items.claim: 10-year yield ~4.9% is at/below the 76-year mean 5.52% (median 4.72%); the 1980s decade averaged a 10.6% yield while the S&P compounded +17%/yr — high long rates have historically coexisted with strong bull markets; what matters is the speed of the rise and whether earnings grow alongside
items.relation: yield at historical norm + rising earnings → no structural multiple crash

SPY.resolution: Khoo's flow/positioning/seasonality evidence (de-grossing, midterms, breadth) argues near-bottom and conflicts with the market prior's very-bearish read (72% Dec hike, 74% ceasefire-break, 44.5% hot CPI). Resolution: the two describe different drivers — Khoo addresses market structure and earnings (short-term flows), not the Fed-rehike/CPI macro regime that the odds encode. We accept the flow evidence as shrinking the severity of downside (bearish, not very-bearish) while keeping policy/geopolitical risk as the dominant constraint. If the Dec hike materializes alongside hot CPI, seasonality historically loses to policy shocks (2018 analogue). The Sep-14 rate-normalcy pattern (1980s analogue: 10.6% decade-average yield with +17%/yr S&P) argues the hawkish-rate regime is survivable for equities while earnings grow; it offsets a fraction of the policy-risk drag — net stance still bearish-leaning.

XLC.resolution: Direct conflict (short-term flow out vs fundamentals intact). Resolution: fundamentals argument applies on a quarters horizon; our 90-day view is dominated by the Fed-hike leg (72%) and the observed outflow — bearish stance kept for the current window; revisit in Q1-2027 when the inventory cash returns and hike risk rolls off. The Oct-14 agentic-disintermediation claim adds a structural (180d half-life) down-leg against the ad-funded members, reinforcing the bearish stance for this window beyond the short-term flow leg.
